task.description:
Design the error recovery improvements for the Expression DSL parser to satisfy DSL-03 (SHOULD): 'On parse error, the parser SHOULD report all errors in a single pass where possible, not stop at the first error.' Acceptance criterion: 'A test input with three distinct syntax errors yields a report with three entries.'

The parser at src/expr/parser.zig already has basic error recovery infrastructure:
- errors: std.ArrayList(ParseError) collects multiple errors
- recordError() appends errors
- synchronize() advances to next sync point (.rparen, .comma, .eof)
- sentinel() returns a null_literal for recovery
- expect() records error and returns null instead of stopping

The design should:
1. Identify any remaining gaps where the parser stops at the first error instead of continuing
2. Specify additional synchronize() calls needed after error recording in each grammar production
3. Define the recovery strategy for each production (where to sync to, what sentinel to produce)
4. Confirm the lexer already collects all errors (it does — errors ArrayList is populated and merged in parse())
5. Verify that the ParseError type in error.zig is sufficient (line, column, token, message)
6. Identify any parser paths where error.is_err short-circuits without recording

Write the design artefact to src/design/dsl-03-error-recovery.md
acceptance_criteria: Design artefact at src/design/dsl-03-error-recovery.md identifies all gap locations in parser.zig
Design specifies sync-after-error strategy for each grammar production
Design covers lexer error merging (already exists, confirm no gaps)
Design is implementable as <= 50 LOC changes to parser.zig plus a test file

result.summary: Design artefact for DSL-03 error recovery: identified 3 gaps (A: dot-path missing synchronize, B: parsePrimary synchronize too aggressive, C: consumeArgList missing synchronize), specified recovery strategies for all grammar productions, verified lexer error merging is complete, confirmed ParseError type is sufficient, and found no error.is_err short-circuit paths. Design is implementable in ~50 LOC.
